newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Malaysian premier sees surge in Asian economies.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian premier sees surge in Asian economies.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Tuesday said East Asia would see strong economic growth in 1997 and overtake Western Europe and North America in the next millennium as the world's biggest regional economy.
"This year, seven of the fastest growing economies in the world will be in East Asia," Mahathir told a two-day Gulf Economic Forum which opened in Bahrain on Tuesday.
"By the time we enter the 21st century, we will almost certainly be the largest regional economy in the world...bigger than Western Europe, bigger than North America," he said.
Bahrain's Finance and National Economy Minister Ibrahim Abdel-Karim, who attended the conference, urged Gulf Arab states to forge close economic links with the booming Asian countries.

"We need to pay increasing attention to our relationships with those economies which are already today -- and which in the next century will continue to be -- a major source of world economic growth...namely the economies of Asia," he said.

Mahathir, who arrived in Bahrain from Kuwait on Monday for a three-day official visit, told the 500 participants at the conference that Malaysian per capita income had risen to $4,374 in 1996 from $227 at the time of independence in 1957.

"I am convinced that the...Far East will increasingly be the centre of economic gravity of this planet. You must resolve to be part of the rise of this new Asia initiated by the East Asian countries," he said.
The gathering was opened by Bahrain's Prime Minister Sheikh Khalifa bin Sulman al-Khalifa who praised the Asian economic approach.

"I call for a study of their (Asian countries) successful economic experiment...to contribute towards our goal of prosperity for everyone and consolidation of the pillars of security and stability," he said.
